predecessors.name: Austria-Hungary
predecessors.text: western Galicia and the Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia

predecessors.name: German Empire
predecessors.text: Posen (Greater Poland) and Pomerelia, the Polish Corridor

predecessors.name: Ukrainian People's Republic
predecessors.text: Eastern Galicia, held by the West Ukrainian People's Republic until July 1919

predecessors.name: Republics of the Soviet Union
predecessors.text: Western Belarus and Western Ukraine, the 1920 shape east of the Bug without Eastern Galicia

successors.name: Nazi Germany
successors.text: the western parts of Poland annexed on 8 October 1939 (the page names no provinces; the Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia and Upper Silesia are the researcher's reading)

successors.name: General Government
successors.text: the remaining block placed 'under the administration of the newly established General Government'

successors.name: Soviet Union
successors.text: eastern Poland up to the line of the rivers Narew, Bug, Vistula and San; the page puts the Soviet areas into the Byelorussian and Ukrainian republics

successors.name: Slovak Republic
successors.text: Gorna Orawa and Tatranska Javorina on Poland's southern border

ledger.x: Late 1918: the Greater Poland uprising.
11 November 1918: Poland is reborn.
1 November 1918: the Polish-Ukrainian War begins in Lwow.
1919: Poland takes western Volhynia.
23 January 1919: Czechoslovakia invades Cieszyn Silesia.
14 February 1919: the Polish-Soviet War begins.
June 1919: the Treaty of Versailles gives Poland the Corridor and Posen.
1919: the Greater Poland uprising ends in Polish hands; the page gives only the span (1918-1919) and the Treaty of Versailles of June 1919.
18 July 1919: Poland wins Eastern Galicia.
18 July 1919: Poland takes Eastern Galicia.
August 1919: the first Silesian Uprising.
Autumn 1920: Zeligowski's mutiny creates Central Lithuania under Polish protection.
Autumn 1920: the Vilnius dispute with Lithuania.
7 May 1920: Poland and its Ukrainian allies take Kyiv.
June 1920: the Soviet counter-offensive.
28 July 1920: the Spa Conference divides Cieszyn Silesia.
28 July 1920: Czechoslovakia receives the larger part of Cieszyn Silesia.
18 March 1921: the Peace of Riga ends the war.
18 March 1921: Riga leaves Poland Western Belarus and Western Ukraine.
24 March 1922: Poland annexes Central Lithuania.
24 March 1922: Central Lithuania ceases to be a separate state, annexed by Poland.
24 March 1922: the de facto end of the fight for Vilnius; Lithuania did not recognise the annexation until after the Polish ultimatum of 1938.
1922: Upper Silesia is partitioned.
1922: the fighting over Upper Silesia ends in the partition (bridged from the German dossier; this page does not date the end).
1 October 1938: Poland annexes Trans-Olza.
1939: Slovakia seizes areas on Poland's southern border.
1 September 1939: Germany invades Poland.
17 September 1939: the Soviet Union invades.
28 September 1939: the German-Soviet line is fixed.
September 1939: eastern Poland falls to the Soviet Union.
6 October 1939: organised resistance ends.
8 October 1939: Germany annexes western Poland.
October 1939: the General Government is set up over the rest.
6 October 1939: the Second Polish Republic ends.

wars.name: Polish-Ukrainian War
wars.outcome: Polish victory: 'Poland won the disputed territory on 18 July 1919'; the Council of Ambassadors incorporated Eastern Galicia into Poland on 14 March 1923.

wars.name: Greater Poland uprising
wars.outcome: Polish insurgents hold Greater Poland; the Treaty of Versailles (June 1919) confirms Poland with the Corridor.

wars.name: Silesian Uprisings
wars.outcome: Three uprisings from August 1919; the partition of 1922 gave Poland the east of Upper Silesia (partition date from the German dossier).

wars.name: Polish-Czechoslovak conflict over Cieszyn Silesia
wars.outcome: Czechoslovak invasion of 23 January 1919, ceasefire of 3 February, Spa division of 28 July 1920 (Czechoslovakia 58.1%).

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War
wars.outcome: Polish victory at Warsaw (12-25 August 1920); the Peace of Riga of 18 March 1921 left Poland Western Ukraine and Western Belarus, about 200 km east of the Curzon Line.

wars.name: Invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: Germany invaded on 1 September, the Soviet Union on 17 September; the partition line was fixed on 28 September and organised resistance ended on 6 October 1939.

certainty.note: The frontiers were being fixed by fighting (Greater Poland, Eastern Galicia, Cieszyn, Upper Silesia, the Soviet front).

Versailles (June 1919), Spa (28 July 1920), Riga (18 March 1921) and the ambassadors' decision of 14 March 1923 fixed the lines; the Lithuanian line (Vilnius) was never recognised by Lithuania until 1938, the Trans-Olza line is a 1938…
The front and the partition line of 28 September are approximate.
